newsitem.title: USA: California lawmakers finalize utility bond measure.
newsitem.headline: California lawmakers finalize utility bond measure.

text.p: California's legislature is expected this week to give final approval to a bill making it easier for the state to issue $7 billion of utility deregulation bonds.

The bonds are part of the state's effort to open its electricity industry to more competition. They will be issued by the state's infrastructure bank, but must be repaid by the investor-owned utilities.
To make it easier for California to market the bonds, Senator Steve Peace introduced a bill earlier this year that will "clean-up" the state's existing utility deregulation law.

Peace's bill will ensure that the bonds retain their state tax-exempt status, and will allow the utilities to collect ratepayer charges beyond the current December 31, 2001 cutoff date, the senator's spokesman said.

"(The clean-up bill) is very important to ensure the best ratings possible for the bonds to save ratepayers in the long-term," said David Takashima, Peace's chief of staff. The changes are expected to save ratepayers an estimated $150 million by lowering bond borrowing costs, he said.
The state Senate approved the clean-up bill last week. It was passed by the Assembly on Monday with minor amendments.
The Senate is scheduled to vote on the amendments Thursday, clearing the way for Gov. Pete Wilson to immediately sign the measure into law.

Consumer advocates -- including Consumers Union and The Utility Reform Network -- had sought to derail the clean-up bill, arguing that the bond plan would shift the cost of nuclear and other uneconomic investments back to consumers.
The state infrastructure bank is expected to come to market with $7 billion of utility bonds in October. The bill authorizes the state to sponsor up to $10 billion of bonds.

The bond proceeds would provide a revenue stream to investor-owned utilities, allowing them to reduce their rates and pay off debt on assets that become less valuable as a result of the electric industry moving into a more competitive market.
PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric and Edison International's Southern California Edison Co plan to issue the first tranche.
